analysis.description: The paper explores the concept of learning an "arrow of time" within the framework of Markov Decision Processes, inspired by the asymmetric progression of time humanly perceived. The study investigates how a learned arrow of time can provide meaningful insights about an environment by measuring reachability, detecting side-effects, and generating intrinsic reward signals. Empirical results are demonstrated across various environments against theoretical models like the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto result.
